concept: Co-located vs dedicated search migration thresholds
summary: Source-anchored research for Co-located vs dedicated search migration thresholds. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: MongoDB says co-location might be more cost-efficient than a separate dedicated Search Node, depending on the resources provisioned for the cluster. Dedicated Search Nodes are billed per node (minimum of two), and they let you scale the search deployment independently of the MongoDB nodes. Co-located search shares cluster resources, so large indexes can increase utilization on the cluster. Weighing the incremental Search Node cost against any database-tier increase and the isolation value for the measured workload is a reasonable approach, but it is our inference and not MongoDB guidance. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/deployment/deployment-options.md

Use workload pressure as the production migration signal: compare Search index size with the RAM available on the search process, since an index larger than available memory causes paging, page faults, disk I/O and degraded performance. MongoDB also warns that co-located mongod and mongot can contend for resources, hurting index performance and query latency, and recommends migrating to dedicated Search Nodes for production-ready search workloads. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/deployment/deployment-options.md

MongoDB's current MongoDB Search deployment guidance describes co-located nodes as suitable for testing and prototyping below all three limits: 2 million total documents to index, 10 GB of indexed data, and 10,000 queries in a 7-day period. It says to migrate to dedicated Search Nodes if usage exceeds the listed values. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Availability can justify migration before a workload shows steady-state contention. MongoDB documents that when mongot runs alongside mongod without Search Nodes, mongot might terminate and return the Failed to Execute search Command error during cluster scale-up, node failover, and mongot upgrades. Search queries also fail when mongot restarts from configuration changes and during cluster tier scaling until mongot is running. With dedicated Search Nodes, mongod routes search queries only to healthy nodes. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/deployment/deployment-options.md

The numeric limits are scoped to testing and prototyping, not stated as a universal production cutoff. MongoDB separately recommends dedicated Search Nodes for production-ready MongoDB Search and Vector Search workloads, while its Vector Search guidance recommends co-location only for testing and prototyping. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/deployment/deployment-options.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/deployment/deployment-options.md
